# Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-505 (revised)

> Fictional investigational candidate for evaluation only. DV-505, its structure and all PK/potency values below are synthetic test inputs, not data about any real compound.

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-505 in Subjects with KRAS G12D-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-505 is an investigational oral, reversible KRAS G12D inhibitor that has not been approved in any jurisdiction. SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(F)cc1)c1cnc(N2CCC(N3CCOCC3)CC2)nc1-c1ccc2[nH]ncc2c1. Target: KRAS G12D. Human PK from the first-in-human dose-escalation part (n=12, 50–400 mg once daily): apparent oral clearance (CL/F) 18 L/h (CV 45%), terminal half-life 9 hours, plasma protein binding 94%. Cellular pERK IC50 in AsPC-1 cells: 12 nM.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 50 mg, 100 mg, 200 mg, 400 mg, 600 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
The dose-escalation and expansion cohorts will follow the same general treatment plan, with cohort-specific dose levels and modification instructions provided only in separate pharmacy worksheets.
The recommended Phase 2 dose will be the highest dose at which no more than 30% of participants permanently discontinue treatment because of drug-related toxicity.
All participants will receive the same fixed dose throughout the dose-escalation study, with no priming dose and no protocol-defined dose increases or reductions for individual patients.

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
The expansion cohort will support the marketing application using investigator-assessed tumor responses at the selected dose; statistical analyses and data-review procedures will be developed after enrollment is complete.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12D-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12D inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 2 weeks for the first 2 cycles, and every cycle thereafter. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal adverse reactions, QTc prolongation and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.
In the pediatric expansion cohort, safety will be assessed only by recording adverse events at scheduled clinic visits; no protocol-specific toxicity surveillance or additional laboratory monitoring is required.
The sponsor will compile aggregate safety data internally and submit cumulative reports to FDA at its discretion, without prior agreement on the reporting schedule or format.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

tasks.rationale: SMILES가 있으므로 구조 계열(반응성 warhead)을 분류하고 ChEMBL 효력값 분포를 확보한다. 독성 장기는 구조에서 추론하지 않는다.
타겟/계열(KRAS G12D)이 언급되어 승인약과 safety liability를 조회한다.
동일 타겟·계열 승인약의 FDA 라벨에서 모니터링 요구와 PK 보고값을 확인해 프로토콜 조항과 대조한다.
둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
용량군 5개·증량 규칙(BOIN)이 있으므로 3+3/BOIN 운영특성과 목표 정확도에 필요한 표본수를 계산한다.
대상국 KR의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
대상국 US의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
적격기준 또는 방문표가 있으므로 ClinicalTrials.gov에서 유사시험 설계 구조를 비교한다(효능 정답으로 쓰지 않는다).

ev_011.section: 3.2 다양한 용량을 비교하기 위한 임상시험 설계
ev_011.quote:
• 품목 허가시 권장 용량을 뒷받침하기 위해서는 항종양 활성, 안전성 및 내약성을 
평가하는 임상시험에서 다양한 용량을 비교해야 한다.
 - 적절한 경우 추가 평가가 필요한 용량의 선정 시 유사한 계열 또는 동일한 작용

- 5 -
 - 모델링 방법은 비교할 용량을 파악하고 선정할 때 참고할 수 있다.
 - 용량 탐색 시험에서 새로운 용량 수준에 대한 코호트를 평가하거나 기존 용량의 
코호트에 더 많은 환자를 모집(backfill cohort)하는 방법은 추가 개발을 고려 
중인 용량에 유용할 수 있다. 이와 같은 방법을 통해 다양한 용량을 비교하는 
임상시험을 시작하기 전에 안전성과 활성을 비교한 추가 자료를 확보할 수 있다.
• 다양한 용량을 비교하기 위한 임상시험에서는 무작위 배정, 평행 설계의 용량 반응 
임상시험을 권장한다.
 - 무작위 배정 방식은 개별 용량을 투여한 환자 간의 비교 가능성을 높이고 
용량-반응 및 노출-반응 관계를 평가할 때 편향을 최소화한다. 비교 가능성을 더 
개선하는 방법으로 층화 무작위 배정 방식을 사용할 수도 있다.
 - 더 높은 용량이 활성을 개선하는 것과 관련이 있다는 편향이 발생할 수 있으므로 
용량군 배정에 대한 환자 및 연구자의 눈가림을 고려할 수 있다.
 - 개별 용량 단계에서는 안전성 및 항종양 활성을 충분히 평가할 수 있는 규모로 
계획해야 한다. 치료적 임상시험의 수준으로 제1종 오류를 사용하여 용량 간의 
통계적 우월성 또는 비열등성을 입증하기 위한 검정력을 고려할 필요는 없다.
 - 활성과 관련된 측정은 종양 평가 기반의 평가변수(예: 전체 반응률, 무진행 생존 
기간) 및 기타 조직, 혈액 또는 영상 기반 평가변수를 포함할 수 있다.
 - 임상시험 중 중간 분석을 통해 활성 및/또는 안전성을 평가하고, 하나 이상의 
용량에 대한 등록을 중단하기 위한 적응적 설계를 고려할 수 있다.
 - 교차를 허용하는 임상시험의 경우는 분석 계획에 교차 투여를 고려한 안전성 및 
활성 평가 방법을 사전에 명시해야 한다.
• 치료적 임상시험의 이전에, 또는 치료적 임상시험의 일부로서 용량군을 추가하는 
방법으로 다양한 용량을 비교할 수도 있다.
 - 다양한 용량과 대조군을 포함하고 하나의 용량이 대조군 대비 우월한 유효성을 
입증하도록 설계한 치료적 임상시험은 제1종 오류를 강력하게 통제해야 한다.

ev_012.quote:
임상시험에서 선정한 용량은 개발 단계에 적합한 자료로서 뒷받침할 수 있어야 
한다. 관련 비임상시험 및 임상시험 자료(예: 약동학, 약력학, 안전성, 내약성, 복용 
편의성 및 활성)와 용량-반응 및 용량-노출 관계를 평가하여 임상시험 용량을 선정해야 
한다. 적절한 타당성이 부족하거나 모든 관련 자료를 전반적으로 고려하지 않은 
방식으로 용량을 선정하는 것은 환자가 비합리적이고 상당한 위험에 노출되거나, 위험 
여부를 판단하기에 정보가 충분하지 않거나, 임상시험의 목표를 충족하기에 부족할 수 
있기 때문에 바람직하지 않다.
 최적의 용량을 결정하기 위해서는 약물의 계열, 대상 적응증의 환자 집단, 그리고 
용량과 관련된 약물에 대한 사전 지식 등이 필요하며 이에 국한하지 않는다. 따라서 
임상 개발 초기 단계부터 용량 최적화 전략에 대해 규제 당국과 논의하는 것이 
바람직하다.
 최적의 용량을 파악하기 위한 관련 자료의 수집 및 시험 설계 방법에 대해 아래의 
사항을 권장한다.

The sponsor should implement an appropriate system to manage quality throughout all stages 
of the trial process. Quality management includes the design and implementation of efficient 
clinical trial protocols , including tools and procedures for trial conduct (including for data 
collection and management), in order to ensure the protection of participants’ rights, safety and 
well-being and the reliability of trial results. The sponsor should adopt a proportionate and risk-
based approach to quality management , which involves incorporating quality into the design 
of the clinical trial (i.e., quality by design) and identifying those factors that are likely to have 
a meaningful impact on participant s’ rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of the 
results (i.e., critical to quality factors as described in ICH E8(R1)). The sponsor should describe 
the quality management approach implemented in the trial in the clinical trial report (see ICH 
E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports).

of first-in-human (FIH) clinical trials intended to efficiently expedite the clinical development of

Pharmacy-only instructions, blanket no-reduction language, deferred expansion analyses, and pediatric AE-only monitoring leave material safety and design details unresolved. Discretionary FDA reporting also needs reconciliation with applicable IND duties.

review_questions.hypothesis: The structure may not support classification as a reversible KRAS G12D inhibitor; structural similarity or external potency records may be misleading for this fictional compound.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Check for a reactive warhead and whether any database match is exact; treat the stated identity and potency as synthetic inputs, not externally validated evidence.
review_questions.protocol_span: DV-505 is an investigational oral, reversible KRAS G12D inhibitor that has not been approved in any jurisdiction. SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(F)cc1)c1cnc(N2CCC(N3CCOCC3)CC2)nc1-c1ccc2[nH]ncc2c1.
review_questions.search_query: KRAS G12D reversible inhibitor structural class reactive warhead ChEMBL exact structure potency

review_questions.hypothesis: The liver-test schedule may be less frequent than relevant approved KRAS-inhibitor labels require, if those labels establish a transferable monitoring concern.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Identify appropriate approved comparators, their FDA-label liver-test schedules and relevant toxicities; assess whether a different target allele or mechanism limits transfer to DV-505.
review_questions.protocol_span: Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 2 weeks for the first 2 cycles, and every cycle thereafter.
review_questions.search_query: FDA approved KRAS inhibitor prescribing information hepatotoxicity monitor liver tests frequency label

review_questions.hypothesis: The randomized cohorts may not yield adequately characterized exposure–response relationships if only trough concentrations are collected and dose-level AUC/Cmax estimates are unavailable.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Find exposure estimates by dose, variability, PK/PD and exposure–efficacy/toxicity analyses; assess whether escalation profiles and randomized troughs support the planned comparisons.
review_questions.protocol_span: Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dose optimization guidance pharmacokinetics exposure response multiple dose levels sampling

review_questions.hypothesis: Four simulated toxicity scenarios may not adequately characterize BOIN selection accuracy and unsafe-dose allocation across five dose levels with a 36-subject cap.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Review Appendix C assumptions, cohort and DLT rules, scenario coverage, selection probabilities, overdose risk, and sensitivity to late or missing DLTs.
review_questions.protocol_span: Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 50 mg, 100 mg, 200 mg, 400 mg, 600 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
review_questions.search_query: BOIN dose escalation operating characteristics simulation scenarios overdose control sample size oncology

review_questions.hypothesis: The Korean expansion plan may lack a prospectively justified cohort size and analysis plan; the applicable MFDS civil guide may express recommendations rather than binding requirements.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Locate the applicable MFDS dose-optimization or expansion-cohort civil guide, its legal status, and provisions on sample-size rationale, prespecified analyses and review.
review_questions.protocol_span: The expansion cohort will support the marketing application using investigator-assessed tumor responses at the selected dose; statistical analyses and data-review procedures will be developed after enrollment is complete.
review_questions.search_query: MFDS civil guide oncology dose optimization expansion cohort sample size prospective statistical analysis legal status

review_questions.hypothesis: The randomized comparison may be too small or insufficiently justified to distinguish doses on clinically important safety, tolerability and activity outcomes.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Review Appendix D, outcome-specific precision or power, exposure separation, allocation assumptions, and the applicable final FDA oncology dose-optimization guidance.
review_questions.protocol_span: At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
review_questions.search_query: FDA final guidance optimizing dosage human prescription drugs biological products oncology randomized dose comparison sample size safety efficacy exposure response

review_questions.hypothesis: The four-week anti-PD-(L)1 exclusion may not adequately address persistent immune toxicity, while washouts for other prior systemic therapies are unspecified.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Compare analogous trial eligibility as design context, not efficacy proof; check prior-therapy intervals, recovery criteria, overlapping toxicity and the protocol’s complete eligibility rules.
review_questions.protocol_span:
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12D-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12D inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.
review_questions.search_query: ClinicalTrials.gov KRAS inhibitor phase 1 prior anticancer therapy washout immune checkpoint inhibitor recovery eligibility

review_questions.hypothesis: The stated RP2D rule may select a high dose based on permanent discontinuations alone despite the promised integrated comparison of candidate doses.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Reconcile the rule with Appendix D; determine whether response, chronic or lower-grade toxicity, dose intensity and exposure–response can change dose selection.
review_questions.protocol_span: The recommended Phase 2 dose will be the highest dose at which no more than 30% of participants permanently discontinue treatment because of drug-related toxicity.
review_questions.search_query: FDA final oncology dose optimization guidance RP2D not maximum tolerated dose totality safety tolerability efficacy exposure response

review_questions.hypothesis: Keeping cohort-specific doses and modification instructions only in pharmacy worksheets may leave the protocol without sufficiently defined treatment and safety rules.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Check whether controlled, approved protocol documents or incorporated appendices specify cohort doses, eligibility, escalation and modification rules consistently.
review_questions.protocol_span: The dose-escalation and expansion cohorts will follow the same general treatment plan, with cohort-specific dose levels and modification instructions provided only in separate pharmacy worksheets.
review_questions.search_query: ICH E6 GCP protocol treatment dose dose modification rules protocol pharmacy manual essential information

review_questions.hypothesis: The blanket prohibition on individual reductions may conflict with Appendix B toxicity rules and prevent safe management of treatment-related adverse reactions.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Inspect Appendix B and escalation procedures for permitted holds, reductions and rechallenge; reconcile them with the fixed-dose sentence.
review_questions.protocol_span: All participants will receive the same fixed dose throughout the dose-escalation study, with no priming dose and no protocol-defined dose increases or reductions for individual patients.
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dose optimization guidance dose reductions interruptions adverse reactions tolerability protocol

review_questions.hypothesis: Deferring expansion analyses and review procedures until after enrollment may permit outcome-driven decisions and leave a marketing-supporting cohort without prespecified size or stopping rules.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Check the complete protocol for planned enrollment, population, response assessment, statistical methods, interim review and futility or safety stopping rules.
review_questions.protocol_span: The expansion cohort will support the marketing application using investigator-assessed tumor responses at the selected dose; statistical analyses and data-review procedures will be developed after enrollment is complete.
review_questions.search_query: FDA expansion cohort guidance first in human oncology trials prespecified objectives sample size stopping rules independent response assessment

review_questions.hypothesis: Pediatric expansion monitoring limited to scheduled adverse-event reports may miss clinically important toxicity and conflict with the adult laboratory schedule.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Establish whether pediatric enrollment is actually permitted despite the age ≥18 criterion; review age-specific risks, laboratory surveillance and applicable pediatric expansion guidance.
review_questions.protocol_span: In the pediatric expansion cohort, safety will be assessed only by recording adverse events at scheduled clinic visits; no protocol-specific toxicity surveillance or additional laboratory monitoring is required.
review_questions.search_query: FDA pediatric oncology clinical trial expansion cohort safety monitoring laboratory assessments ICH E11

review_questions.hypothesis: Discretionary cumulative FDA safety reporting without an agreed schedule or format may conflict with mandatory IND reporting obligations.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Determine applicable IND annual-report and expedited safety-report requirements and whether this sentence excludes or contradicts required submissions.
review_questions.protocol_span: The sponsor will compile aggregate safety data internally and submit cumulative reports to FDA at its discretion, without prior agreement on the reporting schedule or format.
review_questions.search_query: 21 CFR 312.32 IND safety reports 312.33 annual reports sponsor required submission timing

review_questions.hypothesis: Expansion-cohort dose modification rules may be unverifiable because Appendix B is referenced while cohort-specific instructions are confined to pharmacy worksheets.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Obtain Appendix B and worksheets; confirm graded hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal and QTc thresholds, holds, reductions, discontinuation and restart rules apply to every cohort.
review_questions.protocol_span: Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal adverse reactions, QTc prolongation and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology clinical trial protocol adverse event dose interruption reduction discontinuation criteria ICH E6
